title: Helpful Content Review
methodology: Google's Helpful Content guidance (verified fresh in AQ-05D against https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) is qualitative — content quality, expertise/authorship clarity, and people-first focus — not a word-count or keyword threshold. This review reads representative samples directly (not just checking field presence, the gap that let the headline finding below go undetected across four prior content-quality passes) across every published domain.

headline_finding.title: Templated, internal-jargon-leaking sentence construction across 4 of 11 domains, previously undetected
headline_finding.summary: The word "canonical" — internal governance/data-modeling vocabulary (see CANON-001 in docs/FOOD_ONTOLOGY_SUITE_RELEASES.md) — appears verbatim inside consumer-facing summary/seo_description text for 328 of 1,166 leaf entities (28.1%), 56 of 73 groups (76.7%), and 10 of 13 categories (76.9%). It is a reliable proxy for a broader fill-in-the-blank template pattern confirmed by direct reading, not just keyword matching.
headline_finding.example_leaf: Adzuki Bean is a canonical Japanese and East Asian sweet and savory bean ingredient — other legumes use in global pulse cooking pairs with earthy reds, aromatic whites, and spice-friendly rosé.
headline_finding.example_leaf_2: Almond is a canonical marzipan and crusts ingredient — tree nut use in marzipan and crusts cooking pairs with Almondine whites, dry Sherry, and light Pinot Noir.
headline_finding.example_group: Beans — 26 canonical legume ingredients in the Legume Ontology.
why_this_is_more_than_a_word_choice_issu: Grammatically broken construction: 'other legumes use in global pulse cooking pairs with...' and 'tree nut use in marzipan and crusts cooking pairs with...' are subject-verb mismatches — the sentence reads as an unedited template concatenation, not human-reviewed prose.

Non-differentiated wine-pairing conclusion: every one of the 75 legume entries ends with the identical clause 'pairs with earthy reds, aromatic whites, and spice-friendly rosé,' regardless of which specific legume — the single most useful piece of information a food-and-wine-pairing site can offer (which wine, for this specific ingredient) is not actually differentiated for this domain.

No supplementary content to compensate: legume, nut-seed, sweet-flavor, and sauce-condiment (327 of the 328 affected leaf entities) have zero beginner_notes and zero FAQ content — this one templated sentence is the entire narrative experience the page offers, not one weak paragraph among several strong ones.

Propagated into machine-readable and SERP-facing surfaces: AQ-04B correctly wired the authored seo_description field into the HTML <meta name="description"> tag and every JSON-LD description property (an architecturally correct decision, still correct) — but for these 4 domains, seo_description carries the identical jargon-leaking text as summary, meaning the defect now appears in the meta description tag search engines read, not just in on-page prose a casual reader might skim past.
headline_finding.why_four_prior_audits_missed_this: AQ-01/AQ-01R/AQ-01R2's thin-content methodology (TC-01) verified that a narrative summary field is present, non-empty, and rendered — a real and correctly-resolved finding at the time. It did not evaluate whether the sentence construction inside that field was itself templated. AQ-02A's own QA pass verified rendering completeness (1,252/1,252 summaries rendered, 0 empty sections) for the same reason. This is not a case of a prior finding being wrong — TC-01's 'RESOLVED' status is still accurate on its own terms (summaries are present and render) — it's a different, sharper lens (repeatability/template-detection at the sentence-construction level) that none of AQ-01 through AQ-05 applied to this specific field.
headline_finding.scope_precisely_bounded: This is not a site-wide defect. protein (0/210 leaf), cheese (0/204), fruit (0/119), vegetable (0/74), grain-starch (0/76), and fungi (0/43) — 726 of 1,166 leaf entities (62.3%) — have zero instances and, on direct reading, genuinely strong, specific, non-templated prose (examples below). herb-spice has 1 isolated instance (a grammar slip in a single entity, 'Mahleb is an cherry-pit spice' — an article-agreement error, not the group/legume-style systemic template) plus, like the 4 fully-affected domains, no supplementary beginner_notes/FAQ content.
headline_finding.not_a_policy_violation: Correctly classified as a Helpful Content / originality quality concern, not an AdSense Program Policy violation — see reports/adsense-policy-review.json. The content is original (not copied from a third party) and non-deceptive; it is simply poorly constructed for a meaningful share of the site.
headline_finding.not_actionable_within_this_ticket: summary and seo_description are catalog fields (data/*-catalog.json). AQ-06's own regression rules exclude catalog modification regardless of policy justification, and rewriting 328+ sentences responsibly requires domain/editorial judgment this audit should not substitute with a mechanical fix — the same discipline this whole audit chain has held to for every catalog-layer finding since AQ-03. Documented here for a future, scoped editorial pass.

protein.assessment: Strong. Real explanatory sentences with mechanism (e.g., ribeye's marbling/tannin-binding rationale), plus beginner_notes and FAQ present.

cheese.assessment: Leaf prose is clean, concise, factual ('Anthotyro is a fresh sheep's milk cheese from GR (PDO)'), consistent with cheese's shorter-form style. Group-tier summaries do carry the jargon leak — narrower blast radius than the 4 fully-affected domains, but present.

fruit.assessment: Leaf prose is strong and sensorially specific ('Açaí is a Brazilian luxury dark berry with earthy chocolate undertones...'). Group tier affected, same pattern as cheese.

vegetable.assessment: Leaf prose strong and specific (Artichoke's cynarin/wine-sweetness note is genuinely informative, real information gain). Group tier affected.

grain-starch.assessment: Leaf prose strong ('Amaranth is a tiny Aztec pseudocereal with peppery, malty pop...'). Group tier affected.

legume.assessment: Fully affected at every tier. No beginner_notes/FAQ. Highest-severity domain.

nut-seed.assessment: Fully affected at every tier. No beginner_notes/FAQ.

herb-spice.assessment: Leaf prose largely strong; one grammar-error outlier (mahleb). Group tier affected. No beginner_notes/FAQ despite otherwise-strong leaf content — a depth gap distinct from the template-leak issue.

sweet-flavor.assessment: Fully affected at every tier. No beginner_notes/FAQ.

sauce-condiment.assessment: Fully affected at every tier. No beginner_notes/FAQ.

fungi.assessment: Leaf prose strong and specific ('Abalone mushroom is a thick-stemmed Pleurotus prized for seafood-like bite...'). Group tier affected.

other_helpful_content_dimensions.originality: Strong site-wide at the architectural level (every entity has its own authored fields, not a shared boilerplate paragraph) — the headline finding is about construction quality within that per-entity authoring, not about content being copied or shared across entities (except for legume's identical wine-pairing clause, which is a differentiation failure, not literal duplication of a whole sentence).
other_helpful_content_dimensions.educational_value_and_depth: High for protein/cheese (dedicated beginner_notes + FAQ). Moderate for fruit/vegetable/grain-starch/fungi/herb-spice (strong single-sentence summaries, no supplementary depth). Low for legume/nut-seed/sweet-flavor/sauce-condiment (templated single sentence, no supplementary depth) — this is the same 4-domain group as the headline finding, compounding it.
other_helpful_content_dimensions.purpose_and_user_benefit: Clear site-wide: every page states what an ingredient is and how it pairs with wine, serving the site's stated mission directly. Weakened specifically where the pairing conclusion is non-differentiated (legume's identical ending).
other_helpful_content_dimensions.information_gain: Genuine and specific where prose is strong (e.g., artichoke/cynarin, ribeye/tannin-binding) — these are real facts a generic aggregator wouldn't have. Minimal where templated (a legume reader learns almost nothing that distinguishes this legume from another).
other_helpful_content_dimensions.repeatability: This is the core of the headline finding — the legume domain's wine-pairing conclusion is not merely similar but identical across 75 entities, the clearest repeatability signal on the site.
other_helpful_content_dimensions.ai_generated_appearance: The affected domains' summary pattern (rigid slot-fill structure, leaked internal terminology, broken grammar, non-differentiated conclusions) reads exactly like an unedited LLM-template output — whether or not that's literally how it was produced, that is what it would look like to a careful human reviewer or an automated quality classifier.
other_helpful_content_dimensions.template_appearance: Confirmed and quantified above — this is the single most concrete, evidence-backed 'template appearance' finding this entire multi-phase audit chain has produced.

overall_assessment: The site's food-ontology tier is not uniformly excellent — it is genuinely excellent across 6 of 11 domains (protein, cheese, fruit, vegetable, grain-starch, fungi, representing 726 of 1,166 leaf entities) and materially weaker across 4 domains (legume, nut-seed, sweet-flavor, sauce-condiment, 327 entities) plus one narrow herb-spice outlier. This is a Helpful Content quality concern of real, quantified scope — not a policy violation, not a site-wide failure, and not something this audit can or should fix by editing catalog prose itself.
